gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) t FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s WHERE t > (SELECT AVG(t) FROM s)
input: How many customers spent more in total than the average customer's total spend? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT c.Country) FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
input: For each sales support agent, how many distinct countries do their customers live in? Return columns: agent first name, agent last name, country count.

gold_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) mo, SUM(Total) r FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2022' GROUP BY mo), d AS (SELECT mo, r - LAG(r) OVER (ORDER BY mo) inc FROM m) SELECT mo, ROUND(inc, 2) FROM d WHERE inc IS NOT NULL ORDER BY inc DESC LIMIT 1
input: In 2022, which month had the largest revenue increase over the previous month of 2022? Return columns: month as 'YYYY-MM', increase rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN t >= 45 THEN 'Gold' WHEN t >= 40 THEN 'Silver' ELSE 'Bronze' END tier, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) t FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) GROUP BY tier
input: Loyalty tiers: Gold if a customer's lifetime spend is at least 45, Silver if at least 40, otherwise Bronze. How many customers are in each tier? Return columns: tier, count.

gold_sql: SELECT m.Name, ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity * CASE WHEN m.Name LIKE '%Protected%' THEN 0.5 ELSE 1 END), 2) r FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId ORDER BY r DESC LIMIT 1
input: Net revenue counts invoice lines on media types whose name contains 'Protected' at 50% (they are partly refunded) and all other lines at 100%. Which media type has the highest net revenue? Return columns: media type name, net revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) y, i.CustomerId, SUM(i.Total) t FROM Invoice i GROUP BY y, i.CustomerId), r AS (SELECT y, CustomerId, t, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY y ORDER BY t DESC, CustomerId ASC) rn FROM s) SELECT r.y, c.FirstName, c.LastName, ROUND(r.t, 2) FROM r JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = r.CustomerId WHERE rn = 1
input: For each year, which customer spent the most that year (ties broken by the lowest customer id)? Return columns: year as text like '2021', first name, last name, spend rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT r.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.TrackId) n FROM Playlist p JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId JOIN Album a ON a.AlbumId = t.AlbumId JOIN Artist r ON r.ArtistId = a.ArtistId WHERE p.Name = 'Music' GROUP BY r.ArtistId ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
input: Across every playlist named 'Music', which artist has the most distinct tracks? Return columns: artist name, distinct track count.

gold_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT InvoiceDate, SUM(Total) OVER (ORDER BY InvoiceDate, InvoiceId) c FROM Invoice) SELECT date(InvoiceDate) FROM r WHERE c > 1000 ORDER BY c LIMIT 1
input: Ordering invoices by invoice date then invoice id, on which invoice date does the running total of invoice revenue first exceed 1000? Return one column: the date as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

gold_sql: WITH u AS (SELECT t.GenreId g, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2022' THEN il.Quantity ELSE 0 END) a, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2023' THEN il.Quantity ELSE 0 END) b FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY t.GenreId) SELECT gn.Name, ROUND(100.0 * (b - a) / a, 2) p FROM u JOIN Genre gn ON gn.GenreId = u.g WHERE a >= 20 ORDER BY p DESC LIMIT 1
input: Among genres with at least 20 units sold in 2022 (by invoice date), which had the largest percentage growth in units sold from 2022 to 2023? Return columns: genre name, growth percent rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT AlbumId FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT GenreId) = 1)
input: How many albums have all of their tracks in a single genre? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName, c.LastName, CAST(julianday(MAX(i.InvoiceDate)) - julianday(MIN(i.InvoiceDate)) AS INTEGER) d FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY d DESC LIMIT 1
input: Which customer has the most days between their first and last invoice? Return columns: first name, last name, days (integer).

gold_sql: SELECT r.Name, COUNT(*) c FROM Album a JOIN Artist r ON a.ArtistId = r.ArtistId GROUP BY r.ArtistId ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 5
input: Which 5 artists have the most albums? Return columns: artist name, album count.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) >= 3)
input: How many invoices contain tracks from at least 3 different genres? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId WHERE c.FirstName = 'Leonie' AND c.LastName = 'Köhler'
input: What is the total amount spent by the customer named 'Leonie Kohler'? Round to 2 decimals. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) FROM Employee e JOIN Employee s ON (s.EmployeeId = e.EmployeeId OR s.ReportsTo = e.EmployeeId) JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = s.EmployeeId JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
input: For each employee, compute the invoice revenue of the customers they support directly plus the customers supported by their direct reports (one level down). Include only employees with a non-zero result. Return columns: first name, last name, revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName, c.LastName FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE e.FirstName = 'Jane' AND e.LastName = 'Peacock'
input: Which customers are supported by the employee 'Jane Peacock'? Return columns: customer first name, customer last name.

gold_sql: SELECT m.FirstName, m.LastName FROM Employee e JOIN Employee m ON e.ReportsTo = m.EmployeeId WHERE e.FirstName = 'Nancy' AND e.LastName = 'Edwards'
input: Who does the employee 'Nancy Edwards' report to? Return columns: first name, last name of the manager.

gold_sql: SELECT g.Name FROM Genre g WHERE g.GenreId NOT IN (SELECT t.GenreId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL)
input: List genres that have no tracks sold at all (never appear in an invoice line). Return one column: genre name.

gold_sql: WITH g AS (SELECT CustomerId, julianday(InvoiceDate) - julianday(LAG(InvoiceDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerId ORDER BY InvoiceDate, InvoiceId)) d FROM Invoice), c AS (SELECT CustomerId, AVG(d) a FROM g WHERE d IS NOT NULL GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT ROUND(AVG(a), 2) FROM c
input: For each customer, take the average number of days between their consecutive invoices; then average that over all customers with at least 2 invoices. Round to 2 decimals. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY SUM(Total) DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
input: Which billing country has the second-highest invoice revenue? Return columns: country, revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT t.Name, SUM(il.Quantity) u FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId GROUP BY t.TrackId ORDER BY u DESC, t.TrackId ASC LIMIT 5
input: What are the 5 best-selling tracks by number of units sold (sum of invoice line quantity)? Break ties by track id ascending. Return columns: track name, units sold.

gold_sql: WITH al AS (SELECT a.ArtistId, a.AlbumId, COUNT(t.TrackId) n FROM Album a LEFT JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT ArtistId FROM al GROUP BY ArtistId HAVING MIN(n) >= 10)
input: How many artists have at least one album, and every one of their albums has at least 10 tracks? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT g.Name, ROUND(AVG(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) FROM Track t JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
input: What is the average track length in minutes for each genre with at least 100 tracks, rounded to 2 decimals? Return columns: genre name, average minutes.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Customer WHERE CustomerId NOT IN (SELECT i.CustomerId FROM Invoice i JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE g.Name = 'Jazz')
input: How many customers never bought a single 'Jazz' track? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName, c.LastName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId ORDER BY SUM(i.Total) DESC LIMIT 1
input: Which customer spent the most in total? Return columns: first name, last name, total spent rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) FROM Invoice i JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId WHERE g.Name = 'Jazz'
input: How many distinct customers bought at least one 'Jazz' track? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT a.Title, COUNT(*) FROM Track t JOIN Album a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId HAVING COUNT(*) > 25
input: Which albums have more than 25 tracks? Return columns: album title, track count.

gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT r.Name FROM Track t JOIN Album a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId JOIN Artist r ON a.ArtistId = r.ArtistId WHERE t.Milliseconds > 1200000
input: Which artists have at least one track longer than 20 minutes? Return one column: artist name (distinct).

gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(i.Total), 2) FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId WHERE c.Country = 'USA'
input: What is the average invoice total for customers in the USA, rounded to 2 decimals? Use the customer's country. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT Name FROM Track GROUP BY Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT AlbumId) > 2)
input: How many distinct track names appear on more than 2 different albums? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) m, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) FROM Invoice GROUP BY m ORDER BY SUM(Total) DESC, m ASC LIMIT 1
input: Which month (YYYY-MM) had the highest invoice revenue? Return columns: month, revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.Country, c.FirstName, c.LastName, SUM(i.Total) t FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), k AS (SELECT Country FROM Customer GROUP BY Country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) SELECT s.Country, s.FirstName, s.LastName, ROUND(s.t, 2) FROM s WHERE s.Country IN (SELECT Country FROM k) AND s.t = (SELECT MAX(t) FROM s s2 WHERE s2.Country = s.Country)
input: For each country, which customer spent the most? Only include countries with at least 2 customers. Return columns: country, first name, last name, total rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.Composer IS NULL THEN il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity ELSE 0 END) / SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
input: What percent of invoice-line revenue (unit price x quantity) comes from tracks with no composer recorded? Round to 2 decimals. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN g.Name = 'Rock' THEN il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity ELSE 0 END) / SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
input: What percentage of all invoice-line revenue comes from the 'Rock' genre? Round to 2 decimals. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Country) FROM Customer WHERE Company IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(Company) <> ''
input: How many distinct countries have at least one customer with a company name recorded? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT CustomerId FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) BETWEEN '2021' AND '2025' GROUP BY CustomerId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate)) = 5)
input: How many customers have made purchases in every year from 2021 to 2025? Return one column: the count.

gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) || '-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) q, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) FROM Invoice GROUP BY q ORDER BY SUM(Total) DESC LIMIT 1
input: Which calendar quarter had the highest invoice revenue? Return columns: quarter as 'YYYY-Qn' (e.g. '2021-Q3'), revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT Total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Total) rn, COUNT(*) OVER () n FROM Invoice) SELECT ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) FROM o WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
input: What is the median invoice total? (With an even count, average the two middle values.) Round to 2 decimals. Return one column.

gold_sql: SELECT c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId GROUP BY c.CustomerId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 10
input: Which customers bought tracks from more than 10 distinct genres? Return columns: first name, last name, genre count.

gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN BillingCountry = 'USA' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) / SUM(Total), 2) FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2024'
input: For the year 2024, what share of revenue (percent, 2 decimals) came from customers in the USA (by billing country)? Return one column.
